name: Screenplay Studio
description: Narrated, illustrated stories made from a screenplay: the world, its actors and the characters they play, scenes, beats, spoken lines, sounds and the worker queue, with the workflows that make the stills, voice and sound takes and the audio cut.

blueprints.name: Beat
blueprints.description: One beat (unit of meaning) of a story; holds the still brief and camera move.

payload.name: Beat
payload.description: One beat (unit of meaning) of a story; holds the still brief and camera move.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Number
fields.helpText: Zero-padded beat number, 01 to 24.

fields.label: Scene (scene entry slug)
fields.helpText: The scene this beat happens in: pick it from the list (only this story's). It brings the place, light, set dressing and the scene's ambience. On the Timeline a band wraps the beats of one scene. Empty: no scene.

fields.label: Time of day
fields.helpText: When this beat happens, as its scene heading says (INT. CABIN - NIGHT): Night, Dawn, Continuous, Later. The import fills it and the script writes it back into the heading; the same place at another time of day is a new heading.

fields.label: Chapter (chapter entry slug)
fields.helpText: The chapter this beat is in, for a story cut into chapters: pick it from the list (only this story's). Leave empty for a short with none.

fields.label: Cast in frame (cast-member slugs)
fields.helpText: Comma-separated cast-member slugs, e.g. old-ship-cook,pirate-captain. Leave empty for a beat with no lead in frame.

fields.label: Reference pictures (asset slugs)
fields.helpText: Comma-separated asset slugs of the masters the still goes by: the cast in frame, filled from their master. A step reads it as ${entry.data.references}.

fields.label: Expression and action
fields.helpText: What each person is doing and how their face reads. A master's smile wins unless this says otherwise, so be explicit (e.g. mouth a flat line, brows level).

fields.label: Focus prop
fields.helpText: The one prop the frame is about, e.g. the onion.

fields.label: Changes from here on
fields.helpText: What stays changed in every later picture of the story, written as it should look: Valerie has lost her hat; Chet's left sleeve is torn; the lantern is out. The picture of this beat and each beat after it is told. Leave empty when nothing changes.

fields.label: Lead-in (seconds)
fields.helpText: Quiet (or just sound effects) before the first spoken line. Empty: 0.3 s. Lengthen it to let an establishing sound breathe, e.g. waves and gulls over a picture of the ship.

fields.label: Gap between lines (seconds)
fields.helpText: Pause between two spoken lines in this beat. Empty: 0.25 s.

fields.label: Tail (seconds)
fields.helpText: Room after the last spoken line before the next beat. Empty: 0.35 s.

fields.label: Transition into this beat
fields.helpText: How the picture gets into this beat from the one before, replacing the story's setting for this beat only. Empty: the story's. It never changes how long the film is.

fields.label: Transition length into this beat (seconds)
fields.helpText: Empty: the story's length, else 0.5 s.

fields.label: Sound effects
fields.helpText: Sounds under this beat: [{"sound": "<sound slug>", "at": 0, "volume": 0.6}]. `at` is seconds from the start of the beat; volume empty uses the sound's own.

fields.label: Ambience for this beat (sound slug)
fields.helpText: A bed for this beat alone, in place of its scene's: pick a sound of kind ambience (press play to hear it). It plays together with the story's own ambience, which runs under the whole film. Empty: the scene's bed, if any.

fields.label: Ambience level for this beat (0–1)
fields.helpText: Overrides the scene's level for this beat only, e.g. 0.04 when the cabin goes quiet for the letters. Empty: the scene's.

fields.label: Ambience fade in for this beat (seconds)
fields.helpText: Replaces the story's and the sound's fade-in for the bed under this beat. Empty: the story's setting, else the sound's own.

fields.label: Ambience fade out for this beat (seconds)
fields.helpText: Replaces the story's and the sound's fade-out for the bed under this beat. Empty: the story's setting, else the sound's own.

fields.label: The story's ambience in this beat: level (0–1)
fields.helpText: The story's own ambience level for this beat alone, in place of its scene's (0 = silence for the beat). The bed does not stop; it eases to this level and back. Empty: the scene's, else the story's.

fields.label: Music level for this beat (0–1)
fields.helpText: Replaces the scene's and the story's music level while this beat plays. 0 is silence, for a dramatic moment; it eases down and back up over half a second unless this beat sets its fades below. Empty: the scene's, else the story's.

fields.label: Music fade in for this beat (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the music takes to ease to this beat's level as the beat starts (it only matters when the level changes here). Empty: half a second.

fields.label: Music fade out for this beat (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the music takes to ease away from this beat's level as the beat ends, unless the next beat sets its own fade in. Empty: half a second.

fields.label: Notes and sound cues
fields.helpText: What the sheet's Audio cell says that is not speech: a direction ("Hold on the smile"), a note that narration is wanted, and the Sound: cues. Kept so the story's script can be written back from the beats without losing them.

fields.label: Shot (composition from the beat sheet)
fields.helpText: The beat sheet's still / composition line, verbatim. The scene, cast and expression are added to it when the still is made.

fields.label: Fountain
fields.helpText: This beat's own part of the Fountain, exactly as written: its scene heading, action, speeches, notes, synopsis, section line and transition. Made when the Fountain is brought in; the export writes it back. The Picture above is the description made from it.

fields.label: Transition as written
fields.helpText: The transition line written just before this beat (CROSSFADE TO:). Its meaning (a cut, a fade or a dissolve) is set in Transition into this beat.

fields.label: Camera
fields.helpText: A still has no depth, so these are the moves a still can show: the frame moves across the picture or in on it. Replaces the scene's and the story's camera for this beat. Empty: the scene's, else the story's, else a slow push in. A Camera move written out below (the numbers) wins over this. still: the camera does not move; push in: moves in toward the middle: tension, closeness; pull out: moves back to show the surroundings, or isolate; zoom in: a long close in on the middle; zoom out: a long reveal out from the middle; pan left: swings left across the picture; pan right: swings right across the picture; tilt up: pivots up to reveal height; tilt down: pivots down; pedestal up: rises straight up, without tilting; pedestal down: sinks straight down; truck left: slides left alongside the action; truck right: slides right alongside the action; drift: a slow, small float that gives the picture life.

fields.label: Camera move (the numbers)
fields.helpText: The exact move, for when none of the Camera choices is it: `from` and `to` each have x and y (0 to 1: where the view is centred across and down the picture) and zoom (1 = the whole frame, 1.2 = closer). A pan needs zoom above 1 to have room to move. When this is set it wins over the Camera choice. Empty: the Camera choice, else a slow push in. Pick a preset to start from, then adjust.

fields.label: Overlay video
fields.helpText: A picture or video laid over the still of this beat: a PNG with transparency (a framed text card), an animated GIF (words typed out: it plays once and holds its last frame), or a video (rain, dust, film grain: it loops). A GIF's transparency is on or off per pixel, so a WebM or PNG with transparency has smoother edges. An MP4 has no transparency, so use the blend (screen drops black, multiply drops white). Empty: the scene's, else the story's.

fields.label: Overlay blend
fields.helpText: How the video mixes with the still. normal: as it is (a WebM's transparency shows the still through). screen: light parts add, black disappears (rain, sparks, smoke on black). multiply: dark parts darken, white disappears (a vignette, dirt). overlay, lighten, addition: stronger lighting looks. none: no overlay here, even if a scene or the story has one. Empty: normal.

fields.label: Overlay strength (0–1)
fields.helpText: How strongly the overlay shows. Empty: full.

fields.label: Overlay: loop or play once
fields.helpText: loop: starts again when it ends. once: plays through and holds its last frame (typed-out text stays). Empty: a GIF plays once, a video loops.

fields.label: Overlay fade (seconds)
fields.helpText: Fades the overlay in as it starts and out as the beat ends, so it does not pop on. Empty: none.

fields.label: Overlay start delay (seconds)
fields.helpText: Waits this long into the beat before the overlay appears (typed text a moment after the picture). Empty: at once.

fields.label: Info card: label
fields.helpText: A small gold word over the title, like REAL FACT or DID YOU KNOW. Optional.

fields.label: Info card: title
fields.helpText: Makes an info card for this beat: a dimmed picture with the icon, label, title and sentence in the middle, laid over the still. It comes in after Overlay start delay (0.6 s if empty) and fades with Overlay fade (0.35 s if empty). It replaces any overlay the beat, its scene or the story has, for this beat. Empty here and in the sentence: no card.

fields.label: Info card: sentence
fields.helpText: The sentence under the title. A card needs a title or a sentence.

fields.label: Info card: icon
fields.helpText: A small picture above the label (a logo, a symbol). A PNG with transparency sits best. Optional.

fields.label: Info card: backdrop darkness
fields.helpText: How dark the picture goes behind the card, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (black). Empty: 0.5.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Set to queued to make a still for this beat: you are asked to approve the spend, see the picture, then keep it or redo (redo queues it again).

fields.label: Spend approved by a batch
fields.helpText: Set to yes by Make the stills of a story: the one approval already covered this picture, so making it asks nothing more and it is left to be kept afterwards. It becomes used when the making starts, so a later redo asks again.

blueprints.name: Actor
blueprints.description: A person in a world's troupe: the look that stays the same in every role, and a general view picture. Cast them as a character in a story.

payload.name: Actor
payload.description: A person in a world's troupe: the look that stays the same in every role, and a general view picture. Cast them as a character in a story.

fields.label: World (world entry slug)
fields.helpText: The world this actor belongs to, e.g. storyworld.

fields.label: Base
fields.helpText: The general figure it was made from: one of the world's bases (see the world's Bases), e.g. woman, man, girl, boy.

fields.label: Presence
fields.helpText: Voice only for someone heard and never seen (a narrator's actor): no picture is made, a placeholder stands in.

fields.label: Age
fields.helpText: Apparent age in years.

fields.label: Build
fields.helpText: Height and body: what is the same in every role.

fields.label: Hair
fields.helpText: Natural hair (a role can change it with a wig or a cap).

fields.label: General look
fields.helpText: What stays the same in every role: face, proportions, manner. Not costume or props.

fields.label: Distinguishing features
fields.helpText: What picks them out in a lineup (a beard, an earring, a hairstyle). Not costume or props; this is how you find an actor for a role.

fields.label: Baseline wardrobe
fields.helpText: What they wear in the plain actor sheet. A role's costume replaces it; it is not part of who they are.

fields.label: Default voice
fields.helpText: The voice they have unless a character gives another.

fields.label: General view
fields.helpText: The actor in plain base clothes: front, side and back.

fields.label: Views at different ages
fields.helpText: The same person at other ages (and angles), as many as you like. Tag each picture in the Assets library: age-young, age-mid or age-old, plus face-closeup or profile if it is one. Making a Character's master starts from the views tagged for its age.

fields.label: Voice sample
fields.helpText: A short clip of their voice, to hear who they are: ElevenLabs' own preview, a line made in their voice, or your own recording.

blueprints.name: Character
blueprints.description: A character in one story: an actor playing a role, in costume, with the approved master picture.

payload.name: Character
payload.description: A character in one story: an actor playing a role, in costume, with the approved master picture.

fields.label: Cast id
fields.helpText: Stable id, e.g. old-ship-cook.

fields.label: Age (as the script says)
fields.helpText: The age the screenplay gives when it introduces this character: 40s, 20, mid-30s. Filled by the import; it picks Age state below.

fields.label: Sex (as the script says)
fields.helpText: Filled by the import only when the screenplay says it (a pronoun, or a word like boy, woman, lad); empty otherwise. Written into the picture and voice choices by people, never inferred from a name.

fields.label: Speaker name (as written on speech lines)
fields.helpText: The name this character's speech lines use, e.g. captain. The script breakdown joins lines to characters by it.

fields.label: Profile
fields.helpText: The cast/*.json body.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: The story this character is in. A character belongs to one story; the actor may play another character in the next.

fields.label: Actor
fields.helpText: Who plays them.

fields.label: Presence
fields.helpText: Voice only for someone heard and never seen, like a narrator: no picture is needed.

fields.label: Age
fields.helpText: Which age of the actor this Character is. Its master starts from the actor's views tagged age-young, age-mid or age-old to match.

fields.label: Costume
fields.helpText: What they wear and how their hair is done in this story.

fields.label: Props and makeup
fields.helpText: Things they carry or have added for this story (a peg leg is a prop, not part of the actor).

fields.label: Rules for every picture of this character
fields.helpText: What must hold in every picture of this character, and nowhere else: which side a peg leg is on, that the face matches the same person at other ages. The world holds only the style; a rule about one person lives here.

fields.label: Master prompt
fields.helpText: The prompt the master picture is made from. The Casting call writes it with AI from everything known about the role (the actor's sheet, the costume, props and rules, the story and the world's style); read and change it here, and the picture is made from exactly this. Empty it to have it written again.

fields.label: Voice override
fields.helpText: Leave empty to use the actor's voice. Setting the actor fills this from the actor's default voice.

fields.label: Caption colour
fields.helpText: The colour this character's captions are shown in, as six hex digits, e.g. #9ad1ff. Empty: the story's caption colour. It matches by the character's speaker word.

fields.label: Voice sample
fields.helpText: A short clip of this character's voice. Setting the actor fills it from the actor's voice sample; replace it to give the character its own.

blueprints.name: Casting
blueprints.description: A candidate for a role in a story: an actor considered for a character, how well they fit, and the decision.

payload.name: Casting
payload.description: A candidate for a role in a story: an actor considered for a character, how well they fit, and the decision.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Character (character entry slug)
fields.helpText: The role being cast.

fields.label: Actor (actor entry slug)
fields.helpText: The actor being considered: pick one from the troupe.

fields.label: Fit, look, feel and voice
fields.helpText: How well they suit the role.

fields.label: Screen test
fields.helpText: The actor dressed as the character.

blueprints.name: Job
blueprints.description: A heavy task handed to a worker: what to run (kind, args) and how it went. The dispatcher picks up queued jobs, starts a worker for each, and the worker writes the outcome back here.

payload.name: Job
payload.description: A heavy task handed to a worker: what to run (kind, args) and how it went. The dispatcher picks up queued jobs, starts a worker for each, and the worker writes the outcome back here.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: What to run: a kind of job the worker image has (see Job kinds), e.g. audio-cut.

fields.label: Arguments
fields.helpText: The job's own input, e.g. {"story": "the-last-onion"}.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: queued: waiting for the dispatcher. claimed: picked up and being started. running: the worker is on it. done or failed.

fields.label: Result
fields.helpText: What the job produced: asset ids, a timeline, counts.

fields.label: Log
fields.helpText: What happened, and why it failed if it did.

fields.label: Claimed at
fields.helpText: When the dispatcher picked it up (UTC, ISO). A claimed or running job with no progress past its kind's timeout is marked failed.

fields.label: Claimed by
fields.helpText: Which worker took it.

blueprints.name: Job kind
blueprints.description: A kind of job and where it runs: which image does it, how it is started, and how long it may take.

payload.name: Job kind
payload.description: A kind of job and where it runs: which image does it, how it is started, and how long it may take.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: The name jobs ask for, e.g. audio-cut.

fields.label: How it is started
fields.helpText: kubernetes: a Job per run. docker: a container per run on a Docker host. http: sent to a standing worker's URL. local: a process on the dispatcher's own machine.

fields.label: Image
fields.helpText: The container image that does this kind (kubernetes and docker modes).

fields.label: Worker URL
fields.helpText: http mode: the standing worker's address (its /jobs).

fields.label: Resources
fields.helpText: Kubernetes requests and limits, e.g. {"cpu": "1", "memory": "1Gi"}.

blueprints.name: Render Job
blueprints.description: A request to the renderer for a rough cut or final video.

payload.name: Render Job
payload.description: A request to the renderer for a rough cut or final video.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Audio cut
fields.helpText: The stitched sound of the recorded lines (an audio-cut job). Play it, then say where a part needs to change.

fields.label: Timeline
fields.helpText: Where each line sits in the cut: start and end in seconds, with the speech line's slug, so a time you heard maps to the line to change.

blueprints.name: Scene
blueprints.description: A place in a story and everything always in it: the light, the set dressing and the continuity props. Every beat in the scene inherits it.

payload.name: Scene
payload.description: A place in a story and everything always in it: the light, the set dressing and the continuity props. Every beat in the scene inherits it.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry.

fields.label: Place
fields.helpText: What the place is: the structure and layout, from the approved reference photo.

fields.label: Inside or outside
fields.helpText: Whether the scene is inside (INT.), outside (EXT.) or both (INT./EXT.). The import reads it from the scene heading and the script writes it back as one: INT. CAPTAIN'S CABIN. A picture says Interior or Exterior in words, and an interior scene's ambience is muffled by default.

fields.label: Light and time of day
fields.helpText: e.g. daylight through arched windows, warm lantern light.

fields.label: Set dressing (always there)
fields.helpText: Objects that stay on the set for every beat here. Say what is NOT there too (no extra props).

fields.label: Continuity notes
fields.helpText: What carries between beats: where the onion is, what has changed on the table.

fields.label: Camera
fields.helpText: A still has no depth, so these are the moves a still can show: the frame moves across the picture or in on it. The camera for every beat of this scene that does not choose its own. Empty: the story's.

fields.label: Ambience (sound slug)
fields.helpText: The bed that runs under every beat in this scene: pick a sound of kind ambience (press play to hear it). It loops, and crossfades where the place changes. It plays together with the story's own ambience, and a beat's own ambience replaces it for that beat.

fields.label: Ambience level (0–1)
fields.helpText: Loud outside (about 0.7), very low inside (about 0.1). Empty: the sound's own level.

fields.label: Music level (0–1)
fields.helpText: The music's level while this scene plays, in place of the story's (0 = silence for the scene; it eases over half a second at the scene's edges). A beat can set its own. Empty: the story's.

fields.label: Heard from inside (muffled)
fields.helpText: On for an indoor scene: the same sound, low-passed as if through a wall.

fields.label: The story's ambience in this scene: level (0–1)
fields.helpText: The story's own ambience (the waves that run under the whole film) is turned to this level while this scene plays, e.g. 0.1 in the captain's cabin and 0.03 deep in the hold. The bed never stops: its level eases over a second at the scene's edges, so there is no fade out and in per scene. A beat can set its own. Empty: the story's level. This is not this scene's own ambience above, which is a separate bed layered on top.

fields.label: The story's ambience heard from inside (muffled)
fields.helpText: On for an indoor scene: the story's own ambience, low-passed as if through a wall. It eases in and out over a second at the scene's edges, the same sound throughout.

fields.label: Overlay video
fields.helpText: A picture or video laid over the still of every beat in this scene: a PNG with transparency (a framed text card), an animated GIF (words typed out: it plays once and holds its last frame), or a video (rain, dust, film grain: it loops). A GIF's transparency is on or off per pixel, so a WebM or PNG with transparency has smoother edges. An MP4 has no transparency, so use the blend (screen drops black, multiply drops white). Empty: the story's. A beat can set its own.

fields.label: Overlay blend
fields.helpText: How the video mixes with the still. normal: as it is (a WebM's transparency shows the still through). screen: light parts add, black disappears (rain, sparks, smoke on black). multiply: dark parts darken, white disappears (a vignette, dirt). overlay, lighten, addition: stronger lighting looks. none: no overlay here, even if a scene or the story has one. Empty: normal.

fields.label: Overlay strength (0–1)
fields.helpText: How strongly the overlay shows. Empty: full.

fields.label: Overlay: loop or play once
fields.helpText: loop: starts again when it ends. once: plays through and holds its last frame (typed-out text stays). Empty: a GIF plays once, a video loops.

fields.label: Overlay fade (seconds)
fields.helpText: Fades the overlay in as it starts and out as the beat ends, so it does not pop on. Empty: none.

fields.label: Overlay start delay (seconds)
fields.helpText: Waits this long into the beat before the overlay appears (typed text a moment after the picture). Empty: at once.

fields.label: Reference photo id
fields.helpText: The source photo's id (ChatGPT library file) while it lives outside Marvin.

fields.label: Approved illustrated anchor
fields.helpText: The approved painted look of this place. Photos govern structure only.

blueprints.name: Chapter
blueprints.description: One chapter of a long story: a title and the run of beats that belong to it. Each beat names its chapter. On the finished video a chapter is a marker on the timeline (and a line in the YouTube description); in the filmstrip a heading.

payload.name: Chapter
payload.description: One chapter of a long story: a title and the run of beats that belong to it. Each beat names its chapter. On the finished video a chapter is a marker on the timeline (and a line in the YouTube description); in the filmstrip a heading.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the story this chapter belongs to. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Number
fields.helpText: Zero-padded chapter number, 01, 02, ... Chapters play in this order.

fields.label: Summary
fields.helpText: What happens in this chapter, in a line or two (it can become the chapter's line in the video description).

fields.label: Fountain
fields.helpText: This chapter's own part of the story's Fountain, as written (notes and all), made when the Fountain is brought in. Edit it here; the story's Fountain is no longer where the chapters are read from after that.

blueprints.name: Series
blueprints.description: A set of stories (episodes) that share a world, a cast and a premise. Each episode is a story that names its series and its number.

payload.name: Series
payload.description: A set of stories (episodes) that share a world, a cast and a premise. Each episode is a story that names its series and its number.

fields.label: World (world entry slug)
fields.helpText: The world every episode is set in, e.g. storyworld. An episode's own world, if it names one, wins.

fields.label: Premise
fields.helpText: What the series is: the recurring situation, tone and promise to the viewer.

blueprints.name: Shot
blueprints.description: A rendered shot: a still with its focal path and hold.

payload.name: Shot
payload.description: A rendered shot: a still with its focal path and hold.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Focal path
fields.helpText: The move from the renderer manifest.

blueprints.name: Sound
blueprints.description: A reusable sound for any story: what it sounds like and its take. Beats place sounds under their picture; scenes use one as an ambience. Tag it so it can be found again (spoon, kitchen, ambience).

payload.name: Sound
payload.description: A reusable sound for any story: what it sounds like and its take. Beats place sounds under their picture; scenes use one as an ambience. Tag it so it can be found again (spoon, kitchen, ambience).

fields.label: Made for (story slug, optional)
fields.helpText: Where it was first used. A sound belongs to the library, not to a story: any story can use it by naming its slug.

fields.label: What it sounds like
fields.helpText: Describe it plainly: 'gentle waves lapping a wooden ship hull, a few distant seagulls, rigging creaking'.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: How the mix treats it. effect: placed at a moment in a beat. ambience: a bed that loops under a scene. music: a bed under the whole story, faded out at the end. Finer types (the place, the material, the action, the era) are tags.

fields.label: Where the take came from
fields.helpText: generated: ElevenLabs makes it from the description when you queue it. uploaded or recorded: your own file in Take, kept exactly as it is; queueing it never calls ElevenLabs, it only marks it recorded.

fields.label: Length (0.5–30 s)
fields.helpText: Empty: ElevenLabs picks from the description.

fields.label: Loop smoothly
fields.helpText: On for ambience that has to run under a longer beat.

fields.label: Prompt influence
fields.helpText: 0 to 1 (ElevenLabs default 0.3). Higher follows the description more literally, with less variety between takes. Sound effects and ambience only.

fields.label: Model
fields.helpText: The ElevenLabs sound model. Leave empty for its default. Sound effects and ambience only.

fields.label: Fade in (seconds)
fields.helpText: Rise from silence over this long, so the sound does not click on. Empty: none for an effect, the renderer's short crossfade for an ambience, none for music.

fields.label: Fade out (seconds)
fields.helpText: Fall to silence over this long at the end. Empty: none for an effect, the crossfade for an ambience, 2 seconds for music.

fields.label: Take: average level (dB)
fields.helpText: Measured from the take when it is attached: how loud it is on average, in dB below full scale (0 is the loudest a file can be). Around -24 to -14 is comfortable; a bar near the right edge is very loud.

fields.label: Take: loudest moment (dB)
fields.helpText: The loudest instant of the take, in dB below full scale. At 0 it is as loud as a file can go and may be clipped.

fields.label: Volume (0–1)
fields.helpText: How loud this sound is in the mix: the level under the narration (a beat can override it). Listen to the take above, watch its meter, and drag this until it sits right.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Set to queued to make a new take. A generated sound: you are asked to approve the spend, hear the take, then keep it or redo (redo queues it again). An uploaded or recorded sound: your file is kept as it is, nothing is generated.

fields.label: Spend approved by a batch
fields.helpText: Set to yes by Make the sounds of a story: the one approval already covered this sound, so making it asks nothing more and it is left to be kept afterwards. It becomes used when the making starts, so a later redo asks again.

fields.label: Waveform
fields.helpText: The take's loudest and quietest point in each of 240 stretches (audiowaveform JSON), worked out by the worker when a take is attached; the Timeline draws it in the block. Nothing to edit.

blueprints.name: Speech Line
blueprints.description: One spoken line of narration or dialogue, with its recorded audio.

payload.name: Speech Line
payload.description: One spoken line of narration or dialogue, with its recorded audio.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Beat
fields.helpText: The beat (picture) this line is spoken over: pick it from the list (only this story's beats), and Open takes you to the beat. Choose another beat to move the line there; its takes go with it.

fields.label: Character
fields.helpText: The Character (cast member) who speaks this line, by its slug. Filled by the import from the speaker, so a setup can offer just one character's lines (the narrator's, to record them in one sitting). Empty on a line written by hand: it still works, it just is not in a character's list.

fields.label: Text (what is spoken)
fields.helpText: The words the voice says. Fix wording, punctuation or a respelling here, then record again; this is the source of truth, the story script is a readable copy.

fields.label: Fountain
fields.helpText: This speech exactly as written in the Fountain: the cue, its extension, the parentheticals, the marks on the words (*stress*) and any note. Made when the Fountain is brought in.

fields.label: Spoken at the same time as the line before
fields.helpText: Dual dialogue in the Fountain (`^` after the second cue): two people talking at once. Played one after the other unless one take holds both voices, as a mixed recording.

fields.label: Direction
fields.helpText: How this line should sound and feel, in your own words ("tired, a little amused, almost to herself"). Read by people and by Claude when choosing the voice settings and the delivery tags; the voice itself cannot read it.

fields.label: Delivery text
fields.helpText: Optional: the same words with ElevenLabs v3 tags, like [sighs] or [whispers] or [pause]. When filled in, the next take speaks this (on the v3 model) instead of Text. Captions always use Text, never this.

fields.label: Volume (0–1)
fields.helpText: How loud this line is in the mix, whichever take is used: 1 (or empty) is as recorded. A setting of the line, so it applies to every take of it, now and later; the Timeline plays it at this level.

fields.label: Muffled (heard through a wall)
fields.helpText: The highs are cut, as if the line were heard from another room. A setting of the line, so it applies to every take of it. A render applies it (the Timeline's Play cannot).

fields.label: Voice
fields.helpText: The voice that speaks this line (a voice's slug). A new line takes the voice of the story's character with the same speaker. A voice with no ElevenLabs id (your own) is never sent to ElevenLabs either.

fields.label: Where the take came from
fields.helpText: generated: ElevenLabs makes it from the text when you queue the line (you approve the spend). uploaded or recorded: your own take on Audio, kept as it is; queueing it never calls ElevenLabs. Use it for a quick guide take before paying for the real voice: set it to generated and queue the line when you want ElevenLabs.

fields.label: ElevenLabs connection
fields.helpText: The connection that records this line (its slug in Settings -> Integrations). Empty: elevenlabs. Each connection carries its own model, so a second connection set to eleven_v3 (expressive) or eleven_flash_v2_5 (half the cost, for drafts) lets a line pick by name. A line's own Model, if set, still wins over the connection's.

fields.label: Model
fields.helpText: ElevenLabs speech model for this line. Empty: the connection's default (usually eleven_multilingual_v2). eleven_v3 is the most expressive; eleven_flash_v2_5, eleven_turbo_v2_5, eleven_v4_turbo and eleven_v3_conversational cost half as much per character. The workspace's ElevenLabs connection lists every model (action List models). A line with delivery tags (the tagged workflow) always uses eleven_v3.

fields.label: On-screen caption (if different)
fields.helpText: What the caption shows when it should differ from what is spoken. Empty: the caption is the text.

fields.label: Stability (0–1)
fields.helpText: Lower is more expressive, higher more even. Empty: the voice's own setting.

fields.label: Similarity boost (0–1)
fields.helpText: Empty: the voice's own setting.

fields.label: Style (0–1)
fields.helpText: More style is more exaggerated delivery. Empty: the voice's own setting.

fields.label: Speed
fields.helpText: 1 is normal; 0.7–1.2 is the usable range. Slow a line down to give it room.

fields.label: Notes on this take
fields.helpText: What sounded strange and what you changed, so the next take is deliberate.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: Set to queued to make a new take: you are asked to approve the spend, hear the take, then keep it or redo (redo queues it again).

fields.label: Waveform
fields.helpText: The take's loudest and quietest point in each of 240 stretches (audiowaveform JSON), worked out by the worker when a take is attached; the Timeline draws it in the block. Nothing to edit.

blueprints.name: Still
blueprints.description: A source still: its prompt, reference pictures and generated image. Several beats can share one.

payload.name: Still
payload.description: A source still: its prompt, reference pictures and generated image. Several beats can share one.

fields.label: Story (story entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the parent story entry. There is no entry-to-entry relation field, so children hold the parent's slug.

fields.label: Beats served
fields.helpText: List of beat numbers this still serves.

fields.label: References
fields.helpText: Master pictures and the style sheet.

blueprints.name: Story
blueprints.description: A narrated, illustrated story: a screenplay made into a film.

payload.name: Story
payload.description: A narrated, illustrated story: a screenplay made into a film.

fields.label: Setting
fields.helpText: Where and when this story happens: the era, the places, the kind of people. Mood and locations change from story to story, so they live here, not on the world.

fields.label: World (world entry slug)
fields.helpText: The world this story belongs to, e.g. storyworld.

fields.label: Series (series entry slug)
fields.helpText: Slug of the series this story is an episode of. Leave empty for a standalone story.

fields.label: Episode number
fields.helpText: Which episode of the series this is.

fields.label: Cover image
fields.helpText: The story's cover picture. It is the card of the story in the guided setups, so a story is easy to tell apart in a long list.

fields.label: Fountain
fields.helpText: The story, written in Fountain: scene headings (INT. PORCH - DUSK), action, character cues over their dialogue, and `#` section lines where a chapter starts. Write it here, paste it, or have it written for you. For a long script, upload the file instead (Fountain file); the chapters then each keep their own part of it. The guided setup reads it into chapters, beats and spoken lines.

fields.label: Fountain file
fields.helpText: The story's Fountain as a file, for a long script (a feature is about a quarter of a megabyte; there is no limit that matters). Use this or the Fountain text, not both.

fields.label: Credit
fields.helpText: How the writing is credited, e.g. “Written by”. Filled from the Fountain title page when the Fountain is brought in, if empty.

fields.label: Author
fields.helpText: Who wrote it. Filled from the Fountain title page when empty.

fields.label: Source
fields.helpText: What it is based on, e.g. “Original Story”.

fields.label: Contact
fields.helpText: Who to contact about it, as on the title page.

fields.label: Other title page lines
fields.helpText: Any other line of the title page (Format: Short Screenplay), one `key: value` to a line, so nothing is thrown away.

fields.label: Revision
fields.helpText: The number of the last revision applied to the story (0 or empty: none yet). Set when a revision is applied; printed on the script's title page beside the draft date.

fields.label: Revision date
fields.helpText: The day the last revision was applied (2026-11-11). Printed on the script's title page.

fields.label: Title page and front matter, as written
fields.helpText: What the Fountain says before its first beat (the title page, and anything else), exactly as written. The Fountain export writes it back first.

fields.label: Picture shape
fields.helpText: The shape of the finished video. short-9x16: tall, for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikTok (1080x1920). square-1x1: a square feed post. portrait-4x5: the tall feed post Instagram shows biggest (1080x1350). wide-16x9: a regular YouTube video (1920x1080). Your pictures are cropped to fit, so keep the subject in the middle; captions sit lower and closer to the edge on the shapes that are not a tall Short.

fields.label: Where it is going
fields.helpText: Optional. When a render comes out longer than the platform takes, its log says so in plain words (YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels about 3 minutes, TikTok 10, an Instagram feed video 3). Platforms change their limits, so check the current one.

fields.label: Loudness
fields.helpText: How loud the finished sound is, in LUFS (closer to 0 is louder). -14: what YouTube, Instagram and TikTok aim for, so they will not turn it down or up. -16: the default, a little quieter. -23: the broadcast standard.

fields.label: References
fields.helpText: Mood and location pictures for this story. A reference library for people and briefs; nothing attaches them to a picture automatically.

fields.label: Music
fields.helpText: The story's music bed: pick a sound of kind music (press the play button to hear the one chosen). It plays under the whole film at that sound's volume, faded out at the end.

fields.label: Music level (0–1)
fields.helpText: The level of the story's music, under the whole film. A scene can set its own, and a beat its own (the beat's wins, then the scene's, then this). Empty: the music sound's own level.

fields.label: Music fade in (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the music takes to come in at the start of the film. Replaces the film's start fade and the sound's own fade-in, for the music only. Empty: the film's start fade setting, else the sound's own.

fields.label: Music fade out (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the music takes to fade out at the end of the film. Replaces the film's end fade and the sound's own fade-out, for the music only. Empty: the film's end fade setting, else the sound's own, else 2 s.

fields.label: Music under speech
fields.helpText: Lower the music while someone speaks and bring it back in the pauses. none: the music stays where it is. light: down about 9 dB under every line. strong: down about 18 dB, so the music nearly steps aside. It is a set amount whatever the voice's loudness (so with the music at 0.05, strong takes it to about 0.006), and lines closer than 0.7 s apart count as one.

fields.label: Fade out at the end (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the music and the ambience that runs to the end fade out as the film ends, e.g. 3. It covers every bed at once, and it works whatever the length: the render knows where the film ends, even though a spoken line decides how long a picture stays. Empty: the music fades out over 2 s (or its own setting) and the ambience over 0.6 s.

fields.label: Fade in at the start (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the music and the ambience that starts the film fade in as it begins, e.g. 3. Like the fade-out at the end, it replaces the sound's own fade-in for those beds. Empty: the music starts at once (or with its own fade-in) and the ambience fades in over 0.6 s.

fields.label: Ambience (sound slug)
fields.helpText: A bed under the whole film: pick a sound of kind ambience (press play to hear it). It plays together with the ambience of any scene or beat, which layer over it. A scene or a beat can add its own.

fields.label: Ambience level (0–1)
fields.helpText: The level of the story's ambience, under the whole film. Empty: the sound's own level.

fields.label: Ambience fade in (seconds)
fields.helpText: Replaces the sound's own fade-in for every ambience bed in this story (the story's, each scene's and each beat's); a beat can set its own. At the very start of the film the story's fade-in setting above is used instead unless this is set. Empty: each sound's own.

fields.label: Ambience fade out (seconds)
fields.helpText: Replaces the sound's own fade-out for every ambience bed in this story; a beat can set its own. Empty: each sound's own.

fields.label: Ambience under speech
fields.helpText: Lower every ambience bed while someone speaks and bring it back in the pauses, as Music under speech does for the music. none: the beds stay where they are. light: down about 9 dB under every line. strong: down about 18 dB. A set amount whatever the voice's loudness; lines closer than 0.7 s apart count as one.

fields.label: Overlay video
fields.helpText: A picture or video laid over the still of the whole film: a PNG with transparency (a framed text card), an animated GIF (words typed out: it plays once and holds its last frame), or a video (rain, dust, film grain: it loops). A GIF's transparency is on or off per pixel, so a WebM or PNG with transparency has smoother edges. An MP4 has no transparency, so use the blend (screen drops black, multiply drops white). A scene or a beat can set its own.

fields.label: Overlay blend
fields.helpText: How the video mixes with the still. normal: as it is (a WebM's transparency shows the still through). screen: light parts add, black disappears (rain, sparks, smoke on black). multiply: dark parts darken, white disappears (a vignette, dirt). overlay, lighten, addition: stronger lighting looks. none: no overlay here, even if a scene or the story has one. Empty: normal.

fields.label: Overlay strength (0–1)
fields.helpText: How strongly the overlay shows. Empty: full.

fields.label: Overlay: loop or play once
fields.helpText: loop: starts again when it ends. once: plays through and holds its last frame (typed-out text stays). Empty: a GIF plays once, a video loops.

fields.label: Overlay fade (seconds)
fields.helpText: Fades the overlay in as it starts and out as the beat ends, so it does not pop on. Empty: none.

fields.label: Overlay start delay (seconds)
fields.helpText: Waits this long into the beat before the overlay appears (typed text a moment after the picture). Empty: at once.

fields.label: Language
fields.helpText: The spoken language as a code, e.g. en. Empty is English. Used as the transcription language and the voice's language.

fields.label: Pause where a scene ends (seconds)
fields.helpText: Quiet, with the last picture held, added after the last beat of a scene when the next beat is in another scene, e.g. 1. Beats with no scene never get one. It is part of the film's length, so the Timeline shows it. Empty or 0: none.

fields.label: Transition between beats
fields.helpText: How the picture gets from one beat to the next. cut: straight over. fade: down to black and back up. dissolve: one picture melts into the next. It never changes how long the film is: the change happens across the edge of the two beats. A beat can set its own, for the change into that beat.

fields.label: Camera
fields.helpText: A still has no depth, so these are the moves a still can show: the frame moves across the picture or in on it. The camera for every beat that neither it nor its scene chooses. Empty: a slow push in.

fields.label: Transition length (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long a fade or dissolve takes, e.g. 0.5. Empty: 0.5 s. A transition never takes more than half of either beat.

fields.label: Title card text
fields.helpText: The title shown before the first beat, on a plain colour, e.g. the story's name. Leave it empty for no title card. A card is a real part of the film: everything after it starts later, and the Timeline shows it.

fields.label: Title card second line
fields.helpText: A smaller line under the title (optional).

fields.label: Title card length (seconds)
fields.helpText: Empty: 2.5 seconds.

fields.label: End card text
fields.helpText: The words shown after the last beat, e.g. a call to action: Subscribe for the next story. Leave it empty for no end card.

fields.label: End card second line
fields.helpText: A smaller line under it (optional).

fields.label: End card length (seconds)
fields.helpText: Empty: 3 seconds.

fields.label: Card colour
fields.helpText: The background of both cards as six hex digits, e.g. #2b1b12. Empty: near black.

fields.label: Card text colour
fields.helpText: The colour of the words on both cards. Empty: white.

fields.label: Caption style
fields.helpText: How the captions look. classic: white words with a dark outline. box: words on a dark box, easy to read over a busy picture. highlight: the word being said lights up as it is spoken. none: no captions burned in (the subtitle file is still made).

fields.label: Caption position
fields.helpText: Where the captions sit. bottom keeps them clear of the buttons and text YouTube Shorts, Reels and TikTok draw over the lower part of the screen.

fields.label: Caption size
fields.helpText: small, medium or large lettering.

fields.label: Caption colour
fields.helpText: The colour of the words as six hex digits, e.g. #ffffff. Empty: white. A character's own colour (on the Character) replaces it for that speaker.

fields.label: Highlight colour
fields.helpText: For the highlight style: the colour a word turns as it is spoken. Empty: yellow.

fields.label: Chapters to bring in
fields.helpText: Which chapters The guided setup makes: all, one chapter (3), a range (2-4) or a list (1,3,5). Bring them in a piece at a time on a long script.

fields.label: Fountain check
fields.helpText: Written by Check the Fountain: the mistakes in the Fountain the import would read differently from what was meant (a speaker in lower case, a note or a bracket left open, a scene number used twice, a transition without its colon…), each with its line and what to write. Nothing is made; run it again after you fix them.

fields.label: Split plan
fields.helpText: Written by the guided setup: how the Fountain divides into chapters, and what the last run did. Read it before you import. To change the split, add or move the `#` section lines in the Fountain and check the split again.

fields.label: Ready to make?
fields.helpText: Written by the Check a story is ready workflow: what stops a picture or a recording from being made (no World, no actor, no voice) and what is worth a look (no costume, no set dressing). It reads the records only and spends nothing. Run it again after you fix something.

fields.label: Script (PDF)
fields.helpText: The screenplay as a PDF in Courier 12: the one to share or print. Made by the script job.

fields.label: Script (Fountain)
fields.helpText: The screenplay as plain Fountain text, for a screenwriting app. Made by the script job.

fields.label: Script (web page)
fields.helpText: The screenplay as an HTML page. Made by the script job.

fields.label: Script breakdown (web page)
fields.helpText: Who speaks and appears, where, and which sounds, read from the records. Made by the script job.

fields.label: Filmstrip (web page)
fields.helpText: The story's sound with each beat's still, as the render will cut it. Open it in its own tab to play it; approve the beats from the approval it raises. Made by the filmstrip job.

fields.label: Subtitles (file)
fields.helpText: The captions as a subtitle (SubRip) file with their times, made by every whole-story render. Upload it to YouTube, Instagram or TikTok when you would rather they show the captions than burn them in.

fields.label: Video
fields.helpText: The story's rendered video (vertical, narrated, captions burned in). Made by the render job after the filmstrip is approved. By default this is a smaller 720x1280 copy; the full-quality file is kept in the worker's output folder.

fields.label: Sheet log
fields.helpText: One dated line each time the beats were updated from this script: what was added, changed, moved to the Trash, and kept because a picture or recording was made. Written by the import-beats job; do not edit.

blueprints.name: Take
blueprints.description: One recording of a speech line: the audio, how it was made, and your notes on it. A line keeps every take; the one marked In use is what the Audio cut stitches.

payload.name: Take
payload.description: One recording of a speech line: the audio, how it was made, and your notes on it. A line keeps every take; the one marked In use is what the Audio cut stitches.

fields.label: Line
fields.helpText: The speech line this is a take of: pick it from the list (only this story's lines), and Open takes you to the line. The line holds the settings every take of it shares (volume, muffled, the voice), so edit them there.

fields.label: Story
fields.helpText: Slug of the story (copied from the line).

fields.label: Where the take came from
fields.helpText: generated: made by ElevenLabs. uploaded or recorded: your own file, kept as it is. Add one yourself by making a take for the line (Line = the line's slug), attaching the audio, and setting Status to In use and this to uploaded or recorded: the line then uses it.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: draft: not made (you cancelled the spend, or ElevenLabs failed): set it to queued to try again. queued: ElevenLabs is making it (you approve the spend first). recorded: a take that is not the one in use. in_use: the take the line plays; set it to switch the line to this take.

fields.label: Words (what is said)
fields.helpText: The exact text sent to the voice for this take. It starts as the line's Delivery text (with tags) when the line has one, otherwise the line's Text, and you can change it to improvise. With the eleven_v3 model it may carry tags like [sighs] or [whispers].

fields.label: Direction
fields.helpText: How this take should sound, in your own words. A note for people and for Claude; the voice cannot read it. Put tags in Words for the voice.

fields.label: Voice
fields.helpText: The voice used. Starts as the line's (the character's) voice.

fields.label: Model
fields.helpText: The voice model, when it was named (eleven_v3 for tagged takes).

fields.label: Stability
fields.helpText: The setting this take was made with. Empty: the voice's own.

fields.label: Notes on this take
fields.helpText: How it sounds and what to try next time.

fields.label: Audio
fields.helpText: The recording. Upload your own to add a take recorded outside Marvin.

fields.label: Duration (seconds)
fields.helpText: How long the recording is.

fields.label: Waveform
fields.helpText: The take's loudest and quietest point in each of 240 stretches (audiowaveform JSON), worked out by the worker when a take is attached; the Timeline draws it in the block. Nothing to edit.

blueprints.name: Voice
blueprints.description: A speaker's ElevenLabs voice and settings.

payload.name: Voice
payload.description: A speaker's ElevenLabs voice and settings.

fields.label: ElevenLabs voice id
fields.helpText: Needed to speak lines with this voice. A voice added from a clip or a recording has none until it is cloned.

fields.label: Kind
fields.helpText: premade, cloned, generated or professional (as ElevenLabs lists it). Its other labels (gender, age, accent, style) are the voice's tags.

fields.label: Preview
fields.helpText: A short clip of the voice, to hear it.

fields.label: Speaker
fields.helpText: Only on a story's own voice: the name its speech lines use (narrator, cook, captain).

blueprints.name: Worker
blueprints.description: A dispatcher's heartbeat: it rewrites last_seen about once a minute, so Settings → Workers can show whether anything is watching the queue.

payload.name: Worker
payload.description: A dispatcher's heartbeat: it rewrites last_seen about once a minute, so Settings → Workers can show whether anything is watching the queue.

fields.label: Role
fields.helpText: dispatcher

fields.label: Starts
fields.helpText: The modes it starts workers in, e.g. docker, kubernetes.

fields.label: Last seen
fields.helpText: UTC, ISO. Written by the dispatcher about once a minute.

fields.label: Status
fields.helpText: idle or busy.

fields.label: Current job
fields.helpText: The job it is running now, if any.

fields.label: Kinds it can do
fields.helpText: Each kind it offers, with its contract: what it takes (inputs), the media types it accepts, what it produces, and what it needs.

fields.label: Needs / has
fields.helpText: What this machine has that its kinds need, e.g. ffmpeg.

blueprints.name: World
blueprints.description: A world: its premise, the rules of its look, and its place. Stories, actors and characters belong to a world.

payload.name: World
payload.description: A world: its premise, the rules of its look, and its place. Stories, actors and characters belong to a world.

fields.label: Bases
fields.helpText: The general figures actors in this world are made from, one per line: name, then what it is. Each needs a base sheet (front, side, back) to make an actor from.

fields.label: Base sheets
fields.helpText: One sheet per base listed above (front, side, back): what actors are made from.

# Screenplay Studio

Screenplay Studio is the pipeline, not any one world. A **world** (Storyworld is the first; another could be anything) is just records inside it: a `world` entry, its actors, its stories. This skill covers the pipeline; a world's own skill covers its look and its cast.

**In a Marvin workspace the records are the source of truth.** Read references/marvin.md first: what each record holds, the workflows, and the stages from idea to video. Then references/recent.md for what was added later (the readiness check, batch approvals, Fountain checks, the story's ambience bed, recording by character).

- **Writing a Fountain from an idea (or asking an AI to):** read references/fountain.md first. It lists what to decide before writing, the title page (including `Setting:` and `Premise:`), the structure, how to introduce each character, dialogue, pictures, timing, sound and notes, a skeleton, and a check to run before importing. What the file does not say is empty in Marvin.
- **Cutting a Fountain into beats:** the story is one Fountain document (written by you or by an AI) in its Fountain field. The import cuts it with no AI: a `#` section line is a chapter, a scene heading with its first action is a picture, each further action is another, a page break (`===`) always starts a new picture, and each speech is a spoken line. It also makes a Character for each speaker, a Scene for each place and a draft Sound for each sound the words call for. A beat is one picture with its words and sounds, the same as a shot-list row, not a plot beat.
- **One place to edit:** the story's Fountain. Bring it in again after changing it (Refresh adds, updates what nothing has been made from, moves what is gone to the Trash, keeps and flags anything with a picture or recording). The Script job with *version: complete* writes the records back out as a Fountain, and *written* writes the Fountain as it was written.
- **Casting:** read references/actors.md. One actor can play the same person at several ages; tag the actor's views `age-young`, `age-mid`, `age-old` and give each Character an Age.
- **Workers:** one container image, `screenplay-studio-worker`, tagged with the package version it goes with; see docker/README.md in the repository. A queued job that nobody picks up usually means no worker offers its kind: check Settings -> Workers.

Rules that cost time:
- Preview first (`import-beats` and `render` accept a preview), and say what was done in your own words, not only what a job logged.
- Anything that spends credit (images, voices) is asked about first; nothing is published without the author's approval.

# Actors, characters and casting

Three records, kept apart. An **actor** belongs to the *world's troupe*: the look that stays the same in every role. A **character** (`cast-member`) is that actor in **one story**: a role, a costume and props. A **casting** is the search for who plays a role: the candidate actor, how well they fit, a screen test, and whether they were chosen or passed. The same actor can play a different character in the next story. A peg leg or a false beard is a costume or prop of the character, not part of the actor. The narrator can be a **voice-only** character with no picture.

## Bases belong to the world

A *base* is the general figure an actor is made from: proportions and silhouette. A world lists its bases in its `bases` field, each with a base sheet picture (`base_sheets`). Add a base only when making an actor from another one would look wrong (a different body, not a different person). Age within a base is the actor's business.

## The actor record

Fill the `actor` fields from the actor's picture and the brief. Leave a field empty rather than guess; an age is a proposal until the author confirms it.

| Field | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| `title` | the actor's name (the slug is the name in lower case) |
| `world` | the world's slug |
| `base` | one of the world's bases |
| `presence` | `on screen`, or `voice only` for a voice actor (no picture; use a shared featureless placeholder as the `general_view`) |
| `age` | years, only when set |
| `build`, `hair`, `skin_tone` | one line each. Skin tone describes the artwork, not ethnicity |
| `look` | the general look: the face and manner that stay the same |
| `distinguishing_features` | what picks them out in a lineup (a beard, an earring, a hairstyle). Not costume |
| `baseline_wardrobe` | what they wear in the plain sheet. A role's costume replaces it |
| `general_view` | the actor's sheet picture |
| `age_views` | more pictures of the same person at other ages (see below) |
| `voice`, `voice_sample` | their default voice (a voice record's slug) and a clip to hear it |
| `status` | `draft` until the sheet is approved |
| `notes` | anything else that is established |

Do not put story role, family relationships or personality on the actor from how they look. Only established facts are recorded.

**Name the picture file for the actor** (`Nell.png`, not `image-3.png`): in Marvin, "Create entry from asset" turns the file name into the actor's name and slug.

## The character record

A character is made from an actor, not from scratch. Fields: `story`, `actor` (the actor's slug), `role`, `speaker` (the one-word name its speech lines use as the cue in the Fountain), `presence`, `age_state` (young, mid, old), `costume`, `props`, `rules` and `master` (the approved picture). Stills attach the approved master, so an unapproved master blocks them.

**`rules`** is what must hold in every picture of this one character (which side a peg leg is on; that the face matches the same person at other ages). The world holds only the style, so a rule about one person lives here; the still and master workflows put each character's costume, props and rules into the prompt.

## The casting record

`story`, `role`, `character`, `actor` (the candidate), `state` (what the role needs at that point), `fit` (why this actor does or does not fit), `status` (`considering`, `auditioned`, `chosen`, `passed`) and a `screen_test` picture. Search the troupe on the hard fields (presence, base, age range) first, then judge look and voice by eye and ear and write the verdict in `fit`. A role that fits nobody is a gap: make a new actor.

The **Casting call** guided setup (Setups) walks it for one story: pick the world and the story, list the roles (the characters), look through the troupe, shortlist actors for a role (each shortlisted actor is a casting record, with a note on the fit and an optional screen test; mark one Chosen and the others Passed), give the role to the chosen actor with the age and the costume and props, then the role's master picture: an AI writes the prompt from everything known about the role (you read and edit it, it is kept on the role as Master prompt), the picture is made from exactly that prompt, or you upload one made elsewhere (made there it starts from the actor's pictures tagged for the role's age, so tag one `age-young`, `age-mid` or `age-old` first; uploaded it is one you made outside, for example from a prompt the Storyworld characters skill wrote), and approve it. Do the next role by picking it again. The Open call scouts the troupe first; Narrate a story brings in the script and beats.

## Reading what is in Marvin

`marvin platform entries get <slug>` returns an actor's or character's fields and its attached pictures with their URLs. Download the picture to attach it as a reference; do not describe it from memory.

## One actor, many ages (views tagged by age)

An actor has **Views at different ages** (`age_views`): as many pictures of the same person as you like, at other ages and angles. In the Assets library tag each one **`age-young`**, **`age-mid`** or **`age-old`**, and `face-closeup` or `profile` where it is one. A Character (`cast-member`) has an **Age** (`age_state`: young, mid, old). The **`screenplay-make-master`** workflow reads the Character's actor, collects up to four of the actor's pictures tagged for that age, and makes the master from them, the costume and props, and the world's style: it asks before spending image credit, then Keep or Redo, and Keep approves the master.

Rules that keep one man one man across 18, 30 and 52: put the features that never change (brow shape, nose, jaw, a scar, the hair parting) in `distinguishing_features` and keep them in every version; make the young and old masters early and approve them as a pair, side by side; a still takes the approved master, not the raw views (the plain actor sheet fights the costume), except a tagged `face-closeup` when a shot is a reuse of a face. A story that shows the same person at two ages has two Characters pointing at the same actor.

## Writing a master prompt

The **master** is one reference portrait of a character: the actor, as this role, at this age, in this costume. Every still takes it, so the prompt has to pin down the person and the costume, and leave the story out. The image model gets the actor's picture(s) with the prompt; the prompt says what to keep from them and what to change.

1. **Open with the references.** Say the attached picture(s) show the same person and that their face, head shape, eyes, brows, nose, jaw, hair colour and build stay exactly as shown, at the age of the role.
2. **The person.** Age, build, hair, skin and the features that must always be kept, from the actor's sheet. Use the sheet's own words (for example a minimal face with small dark ovals for eyes). Do not infer ethnicity, gender or personality from hair or clothes.
3. **The costume.** Every piece, with colour, material and where it sits, from the character's costume. Say which side something is on when it matters (a ring on the left hand, a cutlass on the left: do not mirror).
4. **Props.** Only what the character wears or holds. Furniture, animals, the place and the weather belong to the stills, not the master.
5. **Pose and frame.** One full-body three-quarter portrait, standing relaxed, on a plain neutral background in even soft light, nothing else in the frame.
6. **The world's style.** Carry the world's style rules: soft, matte, hand-painted miniature rendering, never photographic; heads large and rounded; each hand four fingers and a thumb, never added or dropped; no readable text or writing anywhere.
7. **The character's rules** hold in every picture: put them in as they are written.
8. **Length and form.** 120 to 220 words of plain sentences: no heading, no list, no quotation marks. Use only what is known; leave out what is not. Where the costume and the actor's features disagree, keep the actor's features.
9. **The person's extra instructions** (a softer smile, hands visible) are added last and win over the defaults, unless they break a rule above.

**Guardrails the workflows apply themselves (v130).** The prompt writer is told that the extra instructions may change the person only, so a note that names a place, weather or action ("on a storm-tossed deck") has that part left out; and it writes every side-specific thing as the character's own *anatomical* left or right (a model mirrors "left" otherwise). Whatever the prompt says, *Make the master* adds a fixed closing paragraph, shown in the approval: one character alone on a plain neutral background, no scene, weather, furniture, animals or other people, anatomical sides never mirrored, no writing. A still's prompt says that reference pictures other than a character's own (a place, a style sample, a cover) give the place, light and style only, and nobody who appears only in a reference is drawn.

# Writing the Fountain: from an idea to a file the import reads completely

The story is one Fountain document. The import reads it with no AI and makes the chapters, beats, lines, Characters, scenes and sounds from it, so **what is not in the file is empty in Marvin**. This page says what to write so nothing is missing. Follow it when you write a Fountain from an idea, when an AI writes it, and when you ask an AI to edit one.

## 1. Before writing: answer these

If the idea does not say, decide (or ask) before writing a line. Each answer has a place in the file.

| Answer | Where it goes in the file | Becomes in Marvin |
|---|---|---|
| Title, who wrote it, where it comes from | title page: `Title`, `Credit`, `Author`, `Source` | the story's credits, printed on the script |
| One or two sentences: what the story is about | title page: `Premise:` | the story's **Premise** (the picture workflows read it) |
| Where and when it happens, in one sentence | title page: `Setting:` | the story's **Setting** |
| Format and length | title page: `Format:` | kept with the story |
| Who is on screen: name, age, sex, what they are, what they wear and carry, one thing that marks them | the first action line that brings each in | a **Character** (Role holds the sentences) |
| Who only speaks (narrator, announcer) | `NARRATOR (V.O.)` cue | a voice-only Character (no picture) |
| The places | scene headings | a **Scene** per place |
| What the story sounds like | `[[Sound: …]]` notes, weather words, `~` lyrics | **Sounds** to generate or upload, an **ambience** bed per place |
| What each part is about | `= synopsis` line under each scene heading | the chapter's summary, and the setting if none is given |
| How the story is divided | `# ACT …` lines | **chapters** |

The **World** (which look and rules the pictures follow) is not in the file: choose it on the story in Marvin. The import says when it is missing.

## 2. The title page

First lines of the file, `Key: value`, one blank line after. A value that needs several lines continues on lines indented by four spaces.

```
Title: THE DEVIL'S SHOALS
Credit: Written by
Author: Jared
Source: Original story
Draft date: November 2026
Format: Short Screenplay
Setting: A pirate brigantine wrecked on a cursed reef, one stormy night.
Premise: A ruthless captain and her cabin boy survive a wreck and meet the drowned crews of every ship the reef has taken.
Contact:
    Agent: Blackbeard Literary
    info@example.com
Copyright: (c) 2026 Jared. All rights reserved.
```

`Setting` and `Premise` fill the story's fields when they are empty. Without `Setting:` the import uses the first scene's synopsis, else the first place. **It never invents a premise**: with none, the import names it as missing. Keep every title-page line when an AI edits the file: they are lost easily.

## 3. Structure

- `# ACT I: THE WRECK` starts a **chapter** (use `# ACT II …`, `# ACT III …`, or numbered `## 03 The heist`). Without any `#` line the import cuts chapters by length (about 12 pages each, between two scenes), and a short script is one chapter, whose numbers turn clumsy (`00a`, `00b`…). Keep these lines in every revision.
- `## SCENE 2: THE REEF` is a label, kept as written.
- A scene heading starts a place: `INT. CAPTAIN'S CABIN - NIGHT #2#`. **It must start with `INT.`, `EXT.` or `INT./EXT.`** (or a leading dot, `.UNDERWATER - CONTINUOUS`): `UNDERWATER - CONTINUOUS` is not a scene. Spell a place the same way each time: the same place at another hour is one Scene. The `#2#` number is optional and keeps a scene's identity through revisions.
- Under each heading write one synopsis line: `= Captain Valerie refuses to back down despite the cabin boy's pleas.` It becomes the chapter's summary.

## 4. Characters

Introduce each person **once**, in capitals, the first time they appear in the action, with their age and the sentences that say what they look like. The import copies those sentences into the Character's Role, reads the age and the sex (from the pronouns or a word like *boy*, *woman*, *lad* in them) into the Character's **Age** and **Sex** fields, and sets **Age state** (young under 30, mid under 55, old after) from the age, which picks the actor's picture of that age for the master. A Character made before these fields existed gets them on the next import, only where they are empty.

```
CAPTAIN VALERIE "THE VULTURE" VANE (40s) stands over the desk. She wears a rain-soaked tricorn hat and a long leather coat. One eye is clouded over with a cataract. She jams a compass into her belt.

CHET (20s), a young cabin boy, clutches a waterlogged logbook.
```

- Both `NAME (40s)` and `NAME, 40s,` are read. Use the first.
- Say the sex with a pronoun or a word, say what they wear and carry, and give one mark that tells them apart. **A costume the file never mentions is empty**, and the picture falls back to the actor's own clothes.
- A speaker the file never introduces gets a Character with only a name.
- A narrator or announcer is written `NARRATOR (V.O.)`; someone heard but not seen, `CHET (O.S.)`. Neither is in a picture.

## 5. Dialogue

```
CHET
(shouting over the storm)
The hull is groaning, Captain!

VALERIE
(sneers)
Drop anchor in a graveyard, boy?
```

- A cue is **all capitals, alone on its line**. **Never put a capitals line above action text:** the import makes it a speaker, and that person reads the action aloud. Write a loud word inside a sentence (`a deafening CRUNCH`) and give the sound its own `[[Sound:]]` note: a line that is only capitals is read as a cue or a heading, never as a sound. If a line of capitals must be action, start it with `!` (`!THE PLAGUE OF THE SEA RISES.`).
- A blank line between speakers. No dual dialogue (`^`) unless two voices must overlap.
- The parenthetical is the delivery note (kept with the line).
- A beat holds at most 6 lines; the next starts a new one.

## 6. Pictures, timing and transitions

- Each action paragraph is part of a **picture** (one still). Action right after speech starts a new one. A paragraph is cut after about 420 characters.
- **`===` on its own line always starts a new picture.** Use it when the camera, place or subject changes inside one scene. One picture is one moment, not one per sentence.
- A silent picture plays 4 seconds. To change it: `[[Hold: 1.5s.]]` on its own line inside that picture. A picture with speech lasts as long as the take. Put no pause after every line.
- Transitions go on their own line, in capitals, with a colon: `CUT TO:`, `DISSOLVE TO:`, `CROSSFADE TO:`; the last line may be `FADE OUT.` A transition belongs to the picture that comes after it.
- A title over a picture: `SUPER: THE DEVIL'S SHOALS` as an action line.

## 7. Sound

- Name each sound yourself: `[[Sound: timber grinding against rock at 0.4s.]]` (seconds into the picture; leave `at` off for the start). Describe the **sound**, not the story: "a single sharp splash", not "Chet falls in". When a picture has `[[Sound:]]` notes, only those are made.
- Without a note, the import reads `the sound of X`, `a X sound` and a loud capitalised word, and keeps the sentence as the prompt.
- Lyrics start with `~`; they become one music Sound.
- Rain, thunder, wind and waves in a place's action make its **ambience** bed. Describe the weather once per place.
- The score is a placeholder made for every story: delete it if there is none.

## 8. Notes

`[[ anything ]]` is removed before pictures, narration and subtitles, so it is safe for comments. Only `Hold:` and `Sound:` notes are acted on. A note must have no blank line inside. Do not put story in a note.

## 9. A skeleton

```
Title: …
Credit: Written by
Author: …
Source: …
Draft date: …
Format: …
Setting: …
Premise: …

# ACT I: …

## SCENE 1: …

EXT. PLACE - NIGHT #1#
= One sentence on what this scene does.

Establishing action in one or two sentences. NAME (30s), what they look like and wear.

[[Hold: 2.5s.]]

===

NARRATOR (V.O.)
One spoken line.

NAME
(how it is said)
Their line.

CUT TO:

INT. ANOTHER PLACE - CONTINUOUS #2#
= …

…

FADE OUT.
```

## 10. Check before you hand it over

1. Title page has Title, Credit, Author, Source, Draft date, Format, **Setting** and **Premise**.
2. Every `#` act line is there; every scene heading starts INT./EXT. and has a `=` synopsis.
3. Every person is introduced once, in capitals, with age, a sex word or pronoun, clothes and a mark.
4. No capitals line stands above action; no heading lacks INT./EXT. (the import's report, under **Check:**, names each such line by its number and says how to fix it: a capitals line alone or ending in a full stop is read as a speaker, so start it with `!`; a place-and-time line without INT./EXT. is not a scene)
5. Every silent picture that should not be 4 seconds has a `[[Hold:]]`; every sound that matters has a `[[Sound:]]`.
6. A page break `===` sits wherever the picture must change.
7. **Check it** (next section), then run the import as a **preview**: it reports chapters, beats, lines, Characters, scenes, sounds, and what the story still lacks (World, Setting, Premise), before anything is made.

## 11. Editing a Fountain with an AI

Give the AI this page and say: *keep every title-page line, every `#` act line, every `=` synopsis, every scene number, and every paragraph and line you were not asked to change, word for word*. Unchanged paragraphs keep their picture and recording when the revision is checked; reworded ones are flagged. Ask for the whole file back, as plain text, then make a **Revision** in Marvin: *check* it, read the report, *apply* it. For a rewrite where little of the old text is left, set the revision to `replace`.

## 12. Check it before it is read

The import reads a Fountain the way the format says, and a slip in the writing is not an error to it: a speaker in lower case is action, a note left open is ignored, two scenes with one number are one, a transition without its colon is a line of the story. Each reads fine and means something else. **Check the Fountain** finds those before anything is made, each with its line and what to write, and costs nothing: it reads the text only.

- **In the Narrate a story setup:** the step *Check the Fountain* (then *Read the check*), before the split. It writes the report in the story's **Fountain check**.
- **From the command line, no Marvin needed:** `python -m storyrender check file.fountain` (or `-` for standard input; `--json` for data). It prints what it found and exits 1 when there is something to fix. In the worker image: `docker run --rm -i screenplay-studio-worker python -m storyrender check - < file.fountain`.
- **Through Marvin** (the Marvin CLI, the web app, or an AI over MCP): run the workflow *Screenplay: check some Fountain text* with the text, or *Screenplay: check the Fountain* on a story; both make a `job` of kind `check-fountain` (also queued directly: `args.text`, `args.asset`, or `args.story`). The job's `result` holds `errors`, `looks`, `import_stops`, `report` and `findings`. **An AI writing a Fountain should check it this way before handing it over, fix every error, and check again until there are none.**
- **The import itself** stops on the serious ones (a speaker in lower case that is also written in capitals elsewhere, a note or a bracket left open, a scene number used for two places, a transition with no colon, a Hold or Sound time that is not a number, a section with no title, a heading with no place) and lists them. A preview (dry run) and a revision check only report. To go on anyway, run the import with `accept_errors: yes`. The capitals warnings (a lone line in capitals, a heading with no INT./EXT.) were warnings before and still are.
- **Worth a look, not mistakes:** no title page, no Setting or Premise, a one-word lower-case line above a sentence (a speaker?), a speaker spelled almost like another, characters you cannot see (a non-breaking space pasted in), a stray `===` or `]]`, `>centered<` text.
